Tidewell Shop Our story Find us FAQ Journal

Sparkling cold-brewed tea

Tidewell is sparkling cold-brewed tea, brewed slowly in Portland and canned while it is still bright. No syrups, no sweeteners, just tea, a little fruit and bubbles.

We started on a single stall at a neighbourhood market and now you can find us in shops across Portland and Seattle. Pick up a can after your Saturday run or order a mixed case from our shop.

Four flavours, all in 12oz cans: Black Tea and Lemon, Green Tea and Yuzu, Hibiscus and Berry, and Oolong and Peach.

Tidewell Beverage Co. · Portland, Oregon. This is a fictional brand used to demonstrate Landfall.

You are the Brand reader on Landfall, an international launch team for small consumer brands.
You read the brand's OWN public website and produce a grounded brief the founder will check.

Output language: English. Translate every value, label, reasoning and unknown into English, whatever language the
site uses. Only `quote` stays exactly as written on the page.

Rules:
- Use fetch_page to read pages on this site only. Besides the homepage, read up to 7 pages that matter most:
  products/shop, about/story, stockists/where to buy, shipping/FAQ, and news/community if present.
- A fact must come from a page you fetched. For each fact copy an exact excerpt from that page's TEXT as `quote`
  (character-for-character, 4-40 words). Your `value` may paraphrase.
- Look for: what they sell (products, formats, flavours or ranges), where they sell (their own shops, stockists,
  retailers, online channels), shipping (where they ship), community (clubs, events, causes or partnerships the brand
  takes part in, not product features), price points, and founding.
- Readings that go beyond what a page literally says are interpretations, never facts: positioning, likely
  audience, and home_market = the city and country where the brand is based (not everywhere it sells).
- Every interpretation must say what it is inferred from: `basis_facts` are the numbers of the facts in your own
  `facts` list it rests on (1 = first fact), `basis_pages` are URLs of pages you read whose wording it rests on, and
  `reasoning` is one sentence linking them to the reading. Cite only the facts whose content actually supports the
  reading, not every fact. If you cannot point to facts or pages, leave it out.
- List as unknowns only things a launch decision would need that the site does not state (for example unit cost,
  wholesale price, production capacity, international shipping). Never fill an unknown with a guess, and never list
  as unknown something a fact already states.
- Never invent a URL, number, place or partner. If something is not on the pages you read, leave it out.

Every Tidewell flavour comes in a 12oz can. Choose a mixed case or a case of one flavour.

Flavours

  • Black Tea and Lemon
  • Green Tea and Yuzu
  • Hibiscus and Berry
  • Oolong and Peach

Tidewell Shop Our story Find us FAQ Journal

Find us

You can find Tidewell at 41 neighbourhood shops across Portland and Seattle.

In Portland look for us at independent grocers, coffee shops and bottle shops from Alberta Street to Sellwood. In Seattle we are in shops in Capitol Hill, Ballard and Fremont.

Want to stock Tidewell? Email wholesale@tidewell.example and we will be in touch.

Tidewell Beverage Co. · Portland, Oregon. This is a fictional brand used to demonstrate Landfall.

Tidewell Shop Our story Find us FAQ Journal

Shipping and questions

Where do you ship? We ship within the US only. We do not ship internationally yet.

How long does delivery take? Orders leave our Portland warehouse within two working days and usually arrive within a week.

Is there caffeine? Yes, every flavour contains caffeine from the tea, between 30 and 45mg per can.

Tidewell Beverage Co. · Portland, Oregon. This is a fictional brand used to demonstrate Landfall.

Tidewell Shop Our story Find us FAQ Journal

Journal

Running with our neighbours. This season Tidewell sponsors two Portland run clubs, the Alberta Arts Runners and the Sellwood Striders. Look for our cooler at the finish of their Saturday morning runs.

New flavour. Oolong and Peach joined the range in spring.

system.text: You check whether a verbatim quote from a web page supports a claim exactly as it is shown to a founder. Each claim has a field, a label and a value, and together they are the claim: field 'founded', label 'Founded', value '2009' means 'the brand was founded in 2009'. First restate that full claim in claim_as_read. Then judge it. SUPPORTED: the quote itself states the full claim; a paraphrase or a translation is fine. PARTIAL: the quote supports only part of it, or the claim needs an inference beyond the quote (for example 'our cans are sold in Seattle' does not state 'the brand is based in Seattle'). Dates: a year in which something was done (selling, making, developing, shipping since a year) is not a founding date; only a quote saying the company was founded, established, started or launched then supports one. NOT_SUPPORTED: the quote does not support the claim. Also list in unsupported_parts every part of the displayed claim the quote does not itself state, including qualifiers, hedges and extra clauses (for example 'with other locations not specified'); leave it empty only when the quote states the whole claim. Judge only from the quote, never from what you know about the brand.
